rewrite.noticeThis: Jesus gives the thief three verbs — steal, kill, destroy — an escalating, violent triad. Against them he sets one purpose: "that they may have life." Then he doubles it with a word meaning beyond what is necessary: not just life, but life overflowing.

insight_issue: Ranked: (1) drop the zōē/bios 'kinds of life' framing as lexically decisive — John's zōē is loaded by usage (zōē aiōnios 3:16, 5:24) and by 10:11, where the shepherd lays down his psychē so the sheep may have zōē (unverified); (2) keep the perisson and thysē-triad material unchanged; (3) practice is fine.
